hints.content:
When both factors are whole numbers, then:

$\blueD{\text{factor}} \times \blueD{\text{factor}} = \maroonD{\text{multiple}}$

$\blueD2 \times \blueD6 = \maroonD{12}$

So,

- $\blueD2$ and $\blueD6$ are $\blueD{\text{factors}}$ of $\maroonD{12}$.
- $\maroonD{12}$ is a $\maroonD{\text{multiple}}$ of $\blueD2$ and $\blueD6$.

The true statements are:

- $\maroonD{12}$ is a multiple of $\blueD2$.
- $\maroonD{12}$ is a multiple of $\blueD6$.
